# `silk/text/string`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

UTF-8 text: owned strings, validation of bytes, search, splitting, trimming, and traversal one
Unicode scalar at a time.

## When to use
Use the built-in `string` type for borrowed text, such as a literal or a view into a buffer. Use
[`String`](#String) when the text must own its storage, for example to build text at runtime. Use
`silk.collections.bytes.Bytes` for bytes that are not necessarily UTF-8.

## Details
A `string` and a [`String`](#String) always hold valid UTF-8.

- [`String.fromUtf8`](#String.impl.fromUtf8) checks bytes and borrows them as a `string`. It does not allocate.
- [`String.copyUtf8`](#String.impl.copyUtf8) checks bytes and copies them into a new [`String`](#String).
- [`String.fromBytes`](#String.impl.fromBytes) checks an owned `Bytes` value and keeps its storage, with no copy.
  [`String.intoBytes`](#String.impl.intoBytes) gives the storage back as `Bytes`.

[`String.find`](#String.impl.find), [`String.split`](#String.impl.split), [`String.trim`](#String.impl.trim), and [`String.slice`](#String.impl.slice) search and cut text
without allocation. They return views of the input, and their offsets count UTF-8 bytes.

A failed [`String.append`](#String.impl.append) or [`String.appendOwned`](#String.impl.appendOwned) leaves the string unchanged. Traversal with
[`String.nextScalar`](#String.impl.nextScalar) gives Unicode scalar values and byte offsets. It does not give grapheme
clusters, so one visible character can be more than one scalar.

## Gotchas
A [`ScalarCursor`](#ScalarCursor) is valid only for the string where the traversal started, and only while that
string does not change. Start with [`String.scalarCursor`](#String.impl.scalarCursor) and advance only with
[`String.nextCursor`](#String.impl.nextCursor).

## Examples
### Check bytes as UTF-8
```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.text.string { String, InvalidUtf8 }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let valid = String.fromUtf8(b"Silk") |> Result<string, InvalidUtf8>.unwrapOr("")
  let rejected = String.fromUtf8(b"a\x80") |> Result<string, InvalidUtf8>.unwrapOr("")
  if String.byteLength(valid) != 4 || String.byteLength(rejected) != 0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Count the scalars of a string
```silk
import silk.option { Option }
import silk.text.string { String, ScalarStep }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // "né" has 2 scalars in 3 bytes.
  let text = "né"
  let mut count = 0
  let mut step = String.nextScalar(text, String.scalarCursor())
  while true {
    match move step {
      Option<ScalarStep>.Some { value } => {
        count = count + 1
        step = String.nextScalar(text, String.nextCursor(move value))
      }
      Option<ScalarStep>.None => {
        break
      }
    }
  }
  if count != 2 || String.byteLength(text) != 3 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Build an owned string
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.text.string { String }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut text = run String.copy("hello") |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run String.append(&mut text, ", world") |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if String.view(&text) != "hello, world" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="String"></a>

## `String`

```silk
pub struct String
```

Owned UTF-8 text. Dropping a `String` releases its storage.

### Details

Get a borrowed `string` view with [`String.view`](#String.impl.view). A `String` is affine. Use [`String.copy`](#String.impl.copy) to
make an independent copy of a view. A `String` always holds valid UTF-8. A failed
[`String.append`](#String.impl.append) or [`String.appendOwned`](#String.impl.appendOwned) leaves the string unchanged.

The capacity is the number of UTF-8 bytes that fit before the next allocation. Use
[`String.makeWithCapacity`](#String.impl.makeWithCapacity) or [`String.reserve`](#String.impl.reserve) to allocate before a run of appends.
[`String.clear`](#String.impl.clear) keeps the storage for reuse, and [`String.clearAndFree`](#String.impl.clearAndFree) releases it.

### Gotchas

Traversal with [`String.nextScalar`](#String.impl.nextScalar) gives Unicode scalar values, not grapheme clusters, so one
visible character can be more than one scalar.

<a id="String.impl.fromUtf8Unchecked"></a>

### Associated function `fromUtf8Unchecked`

```silk
pub unsafe fn fromUtf8Unchecked(values: &[u8]) -> string
```

Returns `values` as a `string` view, with no UTF-8 check.

#### When to use

Use this function only when earlier code proves that all of `values` is valid UTF-8, such as a
buffer that this module made. Use [`String.fromUtf8`](#String.impl.fromUtf8) in other cases.

#### Gotchas

This function is `unsafe`. If `values` is not valid UTF-8, the behavior of later text
operations is not defined.

<a id="String.impl.fromUtf8"></a>

### Associated function `fromUtf8`

```silk
pub fn fromUtf8(values: &[u8]) -> Result<string, InvalidUtf8>
```

Checks that `values` is valid UTF-8 and returns it as a `string` view. This function does not
allocate.

#### Details

The view borrows `values` and has the same lifetime.

#### Errors

- [`InvalidUtf8`](#InvalidUtf8) if `values` is not valid UTF-8. `offset` gives the position of the first
  invalid byte.

<a id="String.impl.makeWithCapacity"></a>

### Associated function `makeWithCapacity`

```silk
pub effect fn makeWithCapacity(capacity: usize) -> String ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns an empty `String` with storage for exactly `capacity` UTF-8 bytes.

#### When to use

Use `makeWithCapacity` to build text with appends when its byte length is known or can be
estimated, so that the string allocates once.

#### Details

The capacity counts UTF-8 bytes, not characters. A `capacity` of 0 does not allocate.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the storage.

#### Examples
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.text.string { String }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut text = run String.makeWithCapacity(32) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run String.append(&mut text, "hello") |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  String.clear(&mut text)
  if String.ownedByteLength(&text) != 0 || String.capacity(&text) != 32 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="String.impl.reserve"></a>

### Method `reserve`

```silk
pub effect fn reserve(self: &mut Self, additional: usize) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Makes sure that at least `additional` more UTF-8 bytes fit without another allocation, with
room to spare for later appends. The text does not change.

#### When to use

Use `reserve` before a run of appends whose total is not known. Use [`String.reserveExact`](#String.impl.reserveExact)
when the final byte length is known.

#### Details

If the capacity is already sufficient, this function does nothing. Otherwise, it grows the
capacity by doubling until the bytes fit.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the byte length plus `additional` overflows `usize`, or the
  `Allocator` cannot supply the storage. The string does not change.

<a id="String.impl.reserveExact"></a>

### Method `reserveExact`

```silk
pub effect fn reserveExact(self: &mut Self, additional: usize) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Makes sure that at least `additional` more UTF-8 bytes fit, with no extra capacity. The text
does not change.

#### Details

If the capacity is already sufficient, this function does nothing and does not shrink the
storage. Otherwise, it makes one allocation for exactly the byte length plus `additional`.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the byte length plus `additional` overflows `usize`, or the
  `Allocator` cannot supply the storage. The string does not change.

<a id="String.impl.shrinkToFit"></a>

### Method `shrinkToFit`

```silk
pub effect fn shrinkToFit(self: &mut Self) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Releases the capacity beyond the byte length.

#### Details

If the capacity equals the byte length, this function does nothing. If the string is empty,
it releases the storage. Otherwise, it moves the text into storage for exactly its byte
length.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the new storage. The string does not
  change. An empty string never fails.

<a id="String.impl.fromBytes"></a>

### Associated function `fromBytes`

```silk
pub fn fromBytes(values: Bytes) -> Result<String, InvalidUtf8>
```

Checks that `values` is valid UTF-8 and returns it as a `String` that keeps the same storage.

#### When to use

Use `fromBytes` to turn an owned byte buffer, such as file contents, into owned text without a
copy. Use [`String.fromUtf8`](#String.impl.fromUtf8) to borrow bytes without taking ownership.

#### Details

This function consumes `values`. On success, the `String` keeps the allocation and capacity of
`values`. This function does not allocate and does not copy.

#### Errors

- [`InvalidUtf8`](#InvalidUtf8) if `values` is not valid UTF-8. `offset` gives the position of the first
  invalid byte. The storage of `values` is released.

<a id="String.impl.isCharBoundary"></a>

### Associated function `isCharBoundary`

```silk
pub fn isCharBoundary(value: string, offset: usize) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `offset` is a valid place to cut `value`: the start of a scalar, or the end
of the text.

#### When to use

Use `isCharBoundary` to check an offset before you give it to [`String.slice`](#String.impl.slice), when the
offset does not come from a search such as [`String.find`](#String.impl.find).

#### Details

Offsets count UTF-8 bytes. Offset `0` and offset `String.byteLength(value)` are always
boundaries. An offset after the end gives `false`.

<a id="String.impl.slice"></a>

### Associated function `slice`

```silk
pub fn slice(value: string, offset: usize, length: usize) -> string
```

Returns the `length` bytes of `value` that start at byte `offset`, as a `string` view. This
function does not allocate or copy.

#### When to use

Use `slice` to cut text at offsets from [`String.find`](#String.impl.find), [`String.findLast`](#String.impl.findLast), or
[`String.scalarByteOffset`](#String.impl.scalarByteOffset). Those offsets are always at the start of a scalar.

#### Details

Offsets and lengths count UTF-8 bytes, not characters. The view borrows `value` and has the
same lifetime. `slice(value, String.byteLength(value), 0)` is a valid empty view.

#### Gotchas

The program traps if the range does not fit in `value`, or if `offset` or `offset + length`
falls inside a multi-byte scalar. Check an offset of unknown origin with
[`String.isCharBoundary`](#String.impl.isCharBoundary) first.

#### Examples

##### Take a word out of a sentence

```silk
import silk.text.string { String }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // "é" is two bytes, so "café" ends at byte 5.
  let text = "café au lait"
  if String.slice(text, 0, 5) != "café" || String.slice(text, 6, 2) != "au" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="String.impl.startsWith"></a>

### Associated function `startsWith`

```silk
pub fn startsWith(value: string, prefix: string) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `value` begins with `prefix`. Every text begins with the empty string.

#### Details

The comparison is exact, byte for byte. It does not ignore case and does not normalize
Unicode, so `"é"` written as one scalar does not begin with `"e"`.

<a id="String.impl.endsWith"></a>

### Associated function `endsWith`

```silk
pub fn endsWith(value: string, suffix: string) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `value` ends with `suffix`. Every text ends with the empty string.

#### Details

The comparison is exact, byte for byte. It does not ignore case and does not normalize
Unicode.

<a id="String.impl.contains"></a>

### Associated function `contains`

```silk
pub fn contains(value: string, needle: string) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `needle` occurs anywhere in `value`. Every text contains the empty string.

#### Details

The comparison is exact, byte for byte. It does not ignore case and does not normalize
Unicode. The search compares sixteen bytes at a time on CPUs with 128-bit vectors.

<a id="String.impl.find"></a>

### Associated function `find`

```silk
pub fn find(value: string, needle: string) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the byte offset of the first occurrence of `needle` in `value`, or `None`.

#### Details

The offset counts UTF-8 bytes and is always the start of a scalar, so it can go straight to
[`String.slice`](#String.impl.slice). An empty `needle` occurs at offset `0`. The comparison is exact, byte for
byte, with no case folding or Unicode normalization. The search compares sixteen bytes at a
time on CPUs with 128-bit vectors and does not allocate.

#### Examples

##### Read the value of a setting

```silk
import silk.option { Option }
import silk.text.string { String }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let line = "name = Silk"
  let at = match String.find(line, " = ") {
    Option<usize>.Some { value } => value
    Option<usize>.None => { return 1 }
  }
  let start = at + 3
  let value = String.slice(line, start, String.byteLength(line) - start)
  if at != 4 || value != "Silk" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="String.impl.findLast"></a>

### Associated function `findLast`

```silk
pub fn findLast(value: string, needle: string) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the byte offset of the last occurrence of `needle` in `value`, or `None`.

#### Details

The offset counts UTF-8 bytes and is always the start of a scalar, so it can go straight to
[`String.slice`](#String.impl.slice). An empty `needle` occurs at offset `String.byteLength(value)`. The
comparison is exact, byte for byte, with no case folding or Unicode normalization. This
function does not allocate.

#### Examples

##### Take the extension of a file name

```silk
import silk.option { Option }
import silk.text.string { String }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let name = "archive.tar.gz"
  let dot = match String.findLast(name, ".") {
    Option<usize>.Some { value } => value
    Option<usize>.None => { return 1 }
  }
  let extension = String.slice(name, dot + 1, String.byteLength(name) - dot - 1)
  if extension != "gz" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="String.impl.split"></a>

### Associated function `split`

```silk
pub fn split<'text, 'separator>(value: string<'text>, separator: string<'separator>) -> Split<'text, 'separator>
```

Returns a [`Split`](#Split) that gives the pieces of `value` between occurrences of `separator`, one
at a time.

#### When to use

Use `split` to read fields separated by a comma, words separated by a space, or lines
separated by `"\n"`. Read the pieces with [`Split.next`](#Split.impl.next). Use [`Split.remainder`](#Split.impl.remainder) to take
the rest of the text in one piece, for example the value after the first `=`.

#### Details

The pieces are views of `value`, with its lifetime, and this function does not allocate. A
separator at the start or the end of `value`, or two separators in a row, give an empty piece,
so `"a,,b"` split on `","` gives `"a"`, `""`, and `"b"`, and an empty `value` gives one empty
piece. A [`Split`](#Split) is `Copy`, so copying it starts a second, independent reading.

#### Gotchas

An empty `separator` matches nowhere, so the only piece is all of `value`. Text with Windows
line endings split on `"\n"` keeps a `"\r"` at the end of each line; [`String.trimEnd`](#String.impl.trimEnd)
removes it.

#### Examples

##### Add up comma-separated numbers

```silk
import silk.format { ParseError }
import silk.num.i32
import silk.option { Option }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.text.string { String, Split }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut fields = String.split("4, 5,6", ",")
  let mut total = 0
  while true {
    let field = match Split.next(&mut fields) {
      Option<string>.Some { value } => value
      Option<string>.None => { break }
    }
    total = total + (i32.parse(String.trim(field)) |> Result<i32, ParseError>.unwrapOr(0))
  }
  if total != 15 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="String.impl.trim"></a>

### Associated function `trim`

```silk
pub fn trim(value: string) -> string
```

Returns `value` without the whitespace at its start and its end. This function does not
allocate or copy.

#### Details

Whitespace is every scalar with the Unicode `White_Space` property: the ASCII space, tab, line
feed, vertical tab, form feed, and carriage return, and also U+0085, the no-break space
U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, and U+3000. Whitespace
inside the text stays. The result is a view of `value` with the same lifetime.

#### Examples

##### Clean up a line of input

```silk
import silk.text.string { String }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  if String.trim("\t  hello world \r\n") != "hello world" || String.trim("   ") != "" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="String.impl.nextScalar"></a>

### Associated function `nextScalar`

```silk
pub fn nextScalar(value: string, cursor: ScalarCursor) -> Option<ScalarStep>
```

Reads the scalar at `cursor` in `value`. Returns `None` at the end of the text.

#### Details

A present [`ScalarStep`](#ScalarStep) holds the scalar, its byte position, and the cursor after it. Read
them with [`String.scalarValue`](#String.impl.scalarValue), [`String.scalarByteOffset`](#String.impl.scalarByteOffset), and [`String.nextCursor`](#String.impl.nextCursor). This
function does not allocate.

#### Gotchas

`cursor` must come from [`String.scalarCursor`](#String.impl.scalarCursor) or [`String.nextCursor`](#String.impl.nextCursor) for the same `value`.
A cursor from a different string gives incorrect results.

<a id="Split"></a>

## `Split`

```silk
pub struct Split<'text, 'separator>
```

The pieces of a text between occurrences of a separator, read one at a time. Make one with
[`String.split`](#String.impl.split).

### Details

Each piece is a `string` view of the text that was split, with its lifetime. Read the pieces
with [`Split.next`](#Split.impl.next), or take everything not yet read with [`Split.remainder`](#Split.impl.remainder). A `Split` does not
allocate. It is `Copy`, so a copy reads the remaining pieces again on its own.

<a id="Split.impl.Copy"></a>

## Implementation `Copy for Split<'text, 'separator>`

```silk
impl<'text, 'separator> Copy for Split<'text, 'separator>
```

<a id="Split.impl"></a>

## Implementation `Split<'text, 'separator>`

```silk
impl<'text, 'separator> Split<'text, 'separator>
```

<a id="Split.impl.next"></a>

### Method `next`

```silk
pub fn next(self: &mut Split<'text, 'separator>) -> Option<string<'text>>
```

Returns the next piece of the text, or `None` after the last piece.

#### Details

A piece is the text up to the next separator, without the separator. The last piece is the
text after the last separator, which is empty when the text ends with the separator. Text
with no separator gives one piece: all of the text. The piece is a view with the lifetime of
the text that was split. This function does not allocate.

#### Examples

##### Read the parts of a path

```silk
import silk.option { Option }
import silk.text.string { String, Split }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut parts = String.split("usr/local/bin", "/")
  let mut count = 0
  let mut last = ""
  while true {
    match Split.next(&mut parts) {
      Option<string>.Some { value } => {
        count = count + 1
        last = value
      }
      Option<string>.None => { break }
    }
  }
  if count != 3 || last != "bin" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Split.impl.remainder"></a>

### Method `remainder`

```silk
pub fn remainder(self: &mut Split<'text, 'separator>) -> Option<string<'text>>
```

Returns the text that [`Split.next`](#Split.impl.next) has not given yet, in one piece, and ends the split.

#### When to use

Use `remainder` to split only at the first separator: call [`Split.next`](#Split.impl.next) once for the part
before it, then `remainder` for everything after it, separators included.

#### Details

After `remainder`, [`Split.next`](#Split.impl.next) returns `None`. After the last piece, `remainder` returns
`None`. The text is a view with the lifetime of the text that was split.

#### Examples

##### Split a setting at its first `=`

```silk
import silk.option { Option }
import silk.text.string { String, Split }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut parts = String.split("query=a=b", "=")
  let key = Split.next(&mut parts) |> Option<string>.unwrapOr("")
  let value = Split.remainder(&mut parts) |> Option<string>.unwrapOr("")
  if key != "query" || value != "a=b" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```
